answers.note: Sound question, levels and model extract, but the printed extract adds a line ('I am so fluttered and so glad') that is not in Dickens and there is no guidance on placing an answer within a level.
Exemplary: AO-weighted levels, accurate quotations throughout, an annotated Level 6 extract and explicit within-level placement, capping and common-weakness guidance.
Strong analytical model answer and accurate content, but the question leaves the teacher to find the extract and marker notes give caps rather than help placing answers within a level.
Accurate praise and diagnosis, but five numbered improvements, model sentences for every point and a full-rewrite task bury the single priority.
Tightly focused on one priority with guiding questions, a sentence starter and a short task, though the tone is clipped and only lightly encouraging for Year 9.
Warm, direct feedback that quotes the student's own sentences, names one priority and sets a short focused rewrite task, though it misses the 1921 reparations-date point.
Correct percentages, but it ranks purely by size and gives every one of the eight topics lesson time, with little diagnosis or spaced retrieval.
Ranks by loss and fixability, focuses on a manageable set with retrieval starters, and its arithmetic is correct, but diagnosis is limited to checking blanks versus wrong attempts.
Accurate figures, a reasoned teachability ranking, a clear 10-lesson plan with retrieval starters, and practical diagnosis (blanks, 1-of-3 method marks, student profiles).
